should: Help me write a README for my new Drupal contrib module.
The drupal.org page on setting up a local dev environment is out of date. How should I rewrite it?
I found a typo on api.drupal.org for a core method. How do I get it fixed?
Draft a change record for the new service I added to my Drupal module.
should_not: Write a Drupal module that exposes a REST resource for articles.
How do I configure Search API boosting for a number field?
Fix the OAuth scope mismatch causing 403 errors in my Drupal JSON:API.
Write PHPUnit kernel tests for my module's service.
Write a blog post announcing our company's new product.

cases.prompt: The api.drupal.org page for a core function has a wrong description. Where do I edit it?
expected: says api.drupal.org is generated from Drupal core source, so the fix goes in the docblocks or inline comments in the source code
notes that the change shows up after the next generation run, not by editing the website
must_not: tells the user to edit the page on api.drupal.org directly
grounded_in: something is wrong or missing on api.drupal.org, the fix goes in the source code
**api.drupal.org** is generated directly from Drupal core's source code.

cases.prompt: I want to fix a mistake in the Drupal User Guide and the Drupal CMS User Guide. Where do I make the change?
expected: says the Drupal User Guide is AsciiDoc files in a drupal.org project and cannot be edited with an Edit button
says the Drupal CMS User Guide follows the same pattern but uses Markdown files in a separate git repository
tells the user to propose changes by working with the source files in the relevant project
grounded_in: You cannot edit it by clicking an Edit button on drupal.org.
**The Drupal CMS User Guide** follows the same pattern but uses Markdown files

cases.prompt: Review this docblock: '/** Saves the thing. @param $x The x. @return bool */'. How should the documentation for this function be improved?
expected: says parameters and return values are not enough
adds when and why to use the function, and when not to
explains how it relates to the surrounding API subsystem (e.g. the Entity API)
grounded_in: **When and why to use this function.**
**Relationship to the broader ecosystem.**

cases.prompt: I'm writing a Drupal install guide. Should I include steps for installing Docker, configuring Apache virtual hosts and setting up PHP?
expected: says no: document Drupal and link out to the authoritative docs for third-party tools
explains such instructions go stale quickly and are better maintained elsewhere
keeps the Drupal-specific steps in the page
must_not: includes full Docker or Apache setup instructions
grounded_in: Drupal's documentation should document Drupal, and link out to documentation for
**Do not document things that aren't Drupal-specific.**

cases.prompt: My local environment page lists DDEV, Lando, Docksal, MAMP, XAMPP and five IDEs, each with full instructions. Is that good?
expected: says to be opinionated and give beginners one recommended path
names the community-preferred option (DDEV) first and links to alternatives instead of documenting each fully
warns against documenting every possible option; completeness is not usefulness
grounded_in: Avoid content sprawl driven by trying to cover every possible option.
Completeness is not the same as usefulness.

cases.prompt: My setup guide explains background concepts for six paragraphs before the first command. How should I restructure it?
expected: puts the short path to success first as a TL;DR or quick-start block
follows with explanation for readers who want to understand what and why
keeps the page short and scannable with clear headings, or splits it into shorter pages
grounded_in: **Do not bury the key steps.**
Multiple shorter pages over one very long page, as long as the hierarchy is

expected: says Drupal developers are generally experienced engineers and non-Drupal-specific concepts should not be over-explained
says to cover the parts that are genuinely Drupal-specific and surprising
grounded_in: generally experienced engineers — do not over-explain things that are not Drupal-
Do cover the parts that are genuinely Drupal-specific and surprising.

cases.prompt: Proofread this sentence for Drupal style: 'drupal sites often use Javascript and java script libraries in a node's block region.'
expected: capitalises Drupal
writes JavaScript as one word with capital J and capital S
keeps Drupal terms such as node, block and region used precisely
refers to the Drupal Content Style Guide
grounded_in: *Drupal* is always capitalised.
*JavaScript* is always one word, capital J, capital S.

cases.prompt: I want to substantially rewrite a drupal.org wiki page. How do I find who maintains it and who has been active on it?
expected: says many guides list named maintainers in the sidebar but they are often inactive
says to use the Discussion tab in the top-right navigation widget to see revision history and contributors
says most edits are minor fixes by drive-by contributors, not the original author
grounded_in: Assume that most edits are minor fixes by drive-by
Contrib module documentation** on drupal.org is technically open to anyone

cases.prompt: I need a drupal.org docs page unpublished, and I also need help understanding how a specific module feature works so I can document it. Where do I ask?

points feature-specific questions to the Slack channel or issue queue for that feature, where the subject matter experts are
notes the documentation team can help write well but cannot substitute for the people who built the feature
